messages:
alex: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change the canary on p4d started hitting OOMs for long-context workloads (~8k tokens). noticed during the 02:00 traffic spike.

mira: ugh. which selector change exactly? the one that prefers fused-attn for mid-lengths?

alex: yeah, that one. kernel switch path seems to increase peak workspace allocations. quick profile: 
```
alloc_peak: 41.2GB (before: 32.8GB)
workspace_pool_used: 29GB -> 36GB
kv_promptstore_mem: 4.1GB
promptstore_hit_rate: 0.62 (baseline 0.75)
batch_coalesced: 18% -> 9%
```

cheng: interesting — lower coalescing explains more large temporary buffers. fused kernel path duplicates a few intermediate buffers for perf, which increases transient peak.

luca: second-order effect: selector changes length-estimates per-request, so batching heuristic splits some tokens differently, reducing batch packing. less packing -> more separate large workspaces.

sam: confirming, saw the same on a small perf run: mean workspace size per request jumped ~22%.

mira: can we triage quick mitigations? i'd rather not fully revert if we can cap blowup.

cheng: proposal: 1) hard cap workspace_pool per-GPU (e.g., 28GB) with LRU reclaim. 2) enable buffer_reuse flag for fused kernels so intermediate buffers are recycled instead of reallocated. 3) nudge batching heuristic to prefer pack_density >= 0.65 when kernel = fused.

alex: + add: increase promptstore shard TTL from 3m -> 10m for canary to boost hit rate while we test — that trades memory for fewer reloads.

luca: note on tradeoffs: raising TTL will push promptstore footprint up ~2-3GB on p4d (with our workload sim), but hit rate should go to ~0.80 which reduces rehydration allocations.

sam: quick simulation results (local run): 
```
scenario A: selector=v2, ttl=3m -> peak 41.2GB, hit_rate 0.62
scenario B: selector=v2 + pool_cap 28GB + reuse -> peak 33.5GB, hit_rate 0.64
scenario C: selector=v2 + pool_cap 28GB + reuse + ttl=10m -> peak 30.8GB, hit_rate 0.79
```

mira: those numbers look promising. how invasive is `buffer_reuse` for fused kernels?

cheng: small patch in the allocator wrapper (20 lines), needs QA on correctness for concurrent kernels. risk: subtle aliasing bugs if not careful. i've got a draft.

alex: also found a reproducible trace for the OOM, dumping stack & workspace allocation timeline: 
```
[00:00:00.012] alloc workspace 1: 3.2GB
[00:00:00.014] alloc workspace 2: 5.6GB
[00:00:00.015] fused-kernel temp alloc: 7.8GB
[00:00:00.017] promptstore reload: 2.4GB
[00:00:00.019] total -> OOM
```

luca: thanks — that shows overlap of fused temps and promptstore rehydration. freeing promptstore edge-case before kernel temp alloc would help but is brittle. better to limit peak.

mira: action items?

alex: i'll flip a canary change to set pool_cap=28GB + ttl=10m on the p4d canary. if OOMs stop we keep and roll to other fleets.

cheng: i'll PR buffer_reuse for fused kernels and add tests for aliasing. target EOD.

sam: i'll adjust batching heuristic config to increase pack_density threshold when selector==v2; run 3 synthetic passes.

luca: i'll run a longer 6h sim to confirm steady-state promptstore growth and hit-rate.

sre-bot: alert #2140001234 - OOM rate increased x4 on canary at 2026-03-18T02:12:08Z. link: https://alerts.internal/2140001234

mira: great. assign owners in the ticket and let's meet in 30m if canary still noisy. :+1:

alex: created ticket RDW-8552 and assigned folks. will post canary logs here after the first 10m.

sam: thanks — if pool_cap works we should add a metric for "workspace_cap_pressure" so autoscaler can react before OOMs.

cheng: agreed. i'll add a gauge and emit events when reclaim triggers.

mira: cool. keep edits minimal for the emergency change. no full revert unless needed.

alex: will update in ~10m with canary status.
